name: Bill Shankly
bio: The architect of modern Liverpool. Shankly turned a struggling Second Division side into a relentless First Division powerhouse, winning three league titles, two FA Cups and the UEFA Cup. His bond with the supporters and belief in collective spirit still define Anfield today.

name: Bob Paisley
bio: The most decorated manager in Liverpool's history. Across just nine seasons, Paisley collected six league championships, three European Cups, three League Cups, a UEFA Cup and a UEFA Super Cup — a haul unmatched in English football, achieved with quiet humility and tactical clarity.

name: Kenny Dalglish
bio: Widely revered as Liverpool's greatest ever figure. 'King Kenny' scored the winner in the 1978 European Cup final, orchestrated one of Europe's finest attacks, and later guided the club as player-manager to the historic 1986 League and FA Cup double while standing alongside the city in the aftermath of Hillsborough.

name: Steven Gerrard
bio: The driving heartbeat of Liverpool for 17 seasons. Gerrard dragged his boyhood club back from the brink in the 2005 Champions League final in Istanbul and the 2006 FA Cup final in Cardiff, setting the standard for complete midfield leadership.

name: Ian Rush
bio: Liverpool's all-time record goalscorer with 346 strikes. Equally lethal finishing first time and pressing from the front, Rush won five league titles, three FA Cups and two European Cups, forming an unforgettable partnership with Kenny Dalglish.

name: Robbie Fowler
bio: Christened 'God' by the Kop, Academy graduate Fowler possessed one of the purest natural finishing instincts English football has seen, passing 30 goals in each of his first three full seasons and playing a central part in the 2001 cup treble.

name: Jamie Carragher
bio: Second only to Ian Callaghan on Liverpool's all-time appearance list, Carragher devoted his entire 17-year senior career to Anfield. His defiance in extra time in Istanbul epitomised a defender built on reading of the game, grit and organisational authority.

name: Graeme Souness
bio: The commanding midfield general of Liverpool's most dominant era. Combining fierce competitiveness with effortless passing range, Souness won five league championships and three European Cups, captaining the side to the 1984 treble.

name: Mohamed Salah
bio: The Egyptian King. Salah shattered the 38-game Premier League scoring record with 32 goals in his debut 2017/18 season and remained Liverpool's defining match-winner across nine glittering years. A Champions League winner in 2019 and Premier League champion in 2020 and 2025, he departed in 2026 third on the club's all-time scoring chart.

name: Virgil van Dijk
bio: A transformative presence at the heart of Liverpool's defence since January 2018 and now club captain. Combining composure, aerial dominance and authority, Van Dijk helped deliver the 2019 Champions League and the 2020 and 2025 Premier League titles — becoming the first Dutchman to captain a Premier League-winning side.

name: Jürgen Klopp
bio: The 'Normal One' who reawakened Anfield. Arriving in October 2015, Klopp forged a relentless side that conquered Europe in 2019, lifted Liverpool's first FIFA Club World Cup, and ended a 30-year wait for the league title in 2020, departing in 2024 with every major honour won.

name: Luis Suárez
bio: Few forwards have lit up Anfield with the sheer audacity and intensity of Luis Suárez. His 2013/14 Premier League campaign — 31 goals in 33 appearances without taking penalties — earned the European Golden Shoe and remains one of the finest individual seasons English football has witnessed.

name: Alisson Becker
bio: Signed from AS Roma in 2018, Alisson brought world-class shot-stopping and calm distribution to Liverpool's back line. Winner of the Champions League in 2019 and the Premier League in 2020 and 2025 — and scorer of an unforgettable 95th-minute headed winner at West Brom in 2021 — he stands among the greatest goalkeepers in the club's history.

name: Kevin Keegan
bio: Signed from Scunthorpe United by Bill Shankly in 1971, Keegan became Liverpool's first modern superstar. His telepathic partnership with John Toshack propelled the Reds to three league titles, an FA Cup, two UEFA Cups and a maiden European Cup triumph in Rome in 1977.

name: Jordan Henderson
bio: Succeeding Steven Gerrard as captain was an immense task; Henderson answered it by lifting six different trophies as skipper — the Champions League, UEFA Super Cup, FIFA Club World Cup, Premier League, FA Cup and League Cup — across 12 selfless years at Anfield.

name: John Barnes
bio: Arriving from Watford in 1987, Barnes dazzled Anfield with balance, power and mesmeric dribbling down the left wing. A two-time league champion, two-time FA Cup winner and two-time FWA Footballer of the Year, he remains one of the most gifted players ever to wear the red shirt.
